name: Standing Warm-up
purpose: Gently prepare your body before a short session.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear floor.
safety: Move gently and within a comfortable range. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness or unusual discomfort.
instructions: March gently on the spot for about 30 seconds.
Roll your shoulders slowly forwards and backwards.
Make small, slow arm circles and gradually let them grow if comfortable.
Shift your weight gently from foot to foot.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down; a warm-up should feel easy.
Stay in a range that feels comfortable and never bounce.

limitations: Guided only. The camera does not score warm-up movements.

name: Bodyweight Squat
purpose: Practise a controlled lower-body movement similar to sitting down and standing up.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Use a comfortable range of motion and a clear, stable floor. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness.
instructions: Stand with feet in a comfortable position.
Keep your whole foot supported.
Bend your hips and knees in a controlled way.
Return to standing without rushing.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down so the way down and the way up are both controlled.
Try a slightly wider stance or a smaller depth that keeps your feet supported.
Check your alignment and try a comfortable stance where your knees travel in line with your toes.

limitations: Camera feedback is educational and may be unavailable for some body shapes, clothing, lighting, and camera angles.

name: Hip Hinge
purpose: Learn to bend forward from the hips while keeping your back long.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear floor, with space behind you.
safety: Move slowly within a comfortable range. Stop if you feel pain in your back or legs.
instructions: Stand with feet about hip-width apart and knees softly bent.
Slide your hips backwards as your chest tips forward.
Keep your back long and your neck relaxed.
Bring your hips forward to return to standing.
commonCues: Move only as far as feels comfortable.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Use a smaller range and keep your chest open.
Keep the knee bend small and let your hips travel backwards.

limitations: Instructional only until camera rules are validated. No automated feedback.

name: Push-up
purpose: Practise a controlled upper-body pushing movement using your own body weight.
space: Floor space for your full body length. A sturdy wall or table works for the easier variation.
safety: Choose a variation appropriate to your ability. Stop if you feel pain or unusual discomfort.
instructions: Set up with hands in a comfortable position.
Keep your body supported.
Lower under control only as far as comfortable.
Push back to the starting position.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Try an easier incline variation with hands on a wall or sturdy table, or lower your knees to the floor.
Lower slowly and only as far as feels comfortable.
Breathe steadily throughout the movement.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions and can suggest keeping your hips in line. Turn the phone sideways and place it on the floor side-on or at an angle with your whole body in view; filmed head-on your legs are hidden and it pauses. Experimental.

name: Reverse Lunge
purpose: Practise a controlled single-leg movement: one foot steps back, both knees bend, and you return to standing.
space: About 2 m front to back of clear, stable, non-slip floor. A wall or chair within reach for balance if you need it.
safety: Use a small step and a shallow depth to start. Keep a support within reach if your balance is unsure. Stop if you feel pain in the knees, hips or back, or dizziness.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and land on the ball of that foot.
Bend both knees until the back knee is a hand's width above the floor, or as low as is comfortable.
Press through the front foot to stand up and bring the back foot in.
Repeat on the other side.
commonCues: Step back, then lower straight down.
Front knee in line with your toes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Back knee dropping hard onto the floor
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lower more slowly and stop a little higher; the back knee never needs to touch.
Make the movement smaller and keep the knee travelling over the middle of your foot.
Keep your feet about hip-width apart side to side, as if on two rail tracks.
Keep your chest up and your weight between both feet.

limitations: The camera counts each lunge (either leg) and, side-on, can suggest keeping your chest tall. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Forward Lunge
purpose: Practise stepping forward into a lunge and pushing back to standing, one leg at a time.
space: About 2 m front to back of clear, stable, non-slip floor. A wall or chair within reach for balance if you need it.
safety: Start with a short step and a shallow depth. Keep the front knee over the foot. Stop if you feel pain in the knees, hips or back, or dizziness.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot forward and lower both knees until the back knee is a hand's width from the floor.
Push through the front foot to step back to standing.
Repeat with the other leg.
commonCues: Chest tall, push back with the front foot.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Take a shorter step and keep the knee in line with the toes.
Keep the chest tall and lower straight down.

limitations: The camera counts each lunge (either leg) from how far your hips drop. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Glute Bridge
purpose: Practise lifting the hips from the floor with control while lying on your back.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor where you can lie down.
safety: Lift only as high as is comfortable and keep your neck relaxed on the floor. Stop if you feel pain in your back or neck.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, about hip-width apart.
Rest your arms by your sides, palms down.
Press through your heels and lift your hips until shoulders, hips and knees are roughly in line.
Pause briefly, then lower your hips slowly to the floor.
commonCues: Keep your ribs down; don't arch your back.

commonMistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back at the top
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift a little lower and think of keeping your ribs down.
Move your feet slightly closer and press through the heels.
Keep your knees pointing the same way as your toes.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how far your hips open. Put the phone side-on at floor level with your body in view. Experimental.

name: Forearm Plank
purpose: Practise holding a straight, steady body position on your forearms and toes.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Breathe normally throughout and hold only as long as you can keep good position. Lower your knees to the floor whenever you need to. Stop if you feel pain in your back or shoulders.
instructions: Kneel, then place your forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back one at a time onto your toes.
Hold one straight line from head to heels.
Breathe steadily; lower your knees to rest when you need to.
commonCues: One straight line from head to heels.
Knees down to rest whenever you need.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Squeeze your glutes gently, or rest on your knees and hold a shorter time.
Lower your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Breathe slowly in and out through the hold.

limitations: The camera times your hold only while you're in the position (body long and level, elbows under your shoulders), and may suggest lifting or lowering your hips into one line; it does not judge effort or how long you should hold. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Step Jack
purpose: A low-impact version of the jumping jack: step to the side while the arms sweep overhead, to warm up and raise the heart rate.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear floor with room to reach overhead.
safety: Keep a comfortable pace and stop if you feel dizzy, short of breath or unwell. Check there is nothing above or beside you before raising your arms.
instructions: Stand with your feet close together and arms by your sides.
Step one foot out to the side as both arms sweep up overhead.
Bring the foot back in as the arms come down.
Alternate sides at a steady rhythm.
commonCues: Step out, arms up; step in, arms down.
Land softly on the stepping foot.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down until each step lands where you want it.

commonMistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
commonMistakes.adjustment: Reach long through the arms and keep the neck relaxed.

limitations: The camera counts each step jack from your arms going overhead. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Calf Raise
purpose: Practise rising onto the balls of the feet and lowering with control.
space: A small area of stable floor, next to a wall or chair you can touch for balance.
safety: Hold a support lightly if your balance is unsure. Stop if you feel pain in your feet, ankles or calves.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Rise onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels.
Pause at the top.
Lower your heels slowly back to the floor.
commonCues: Weight over the big toe and second toe.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep your weight toward the big toe side of the foot.
Pause with your heels down before the next rise.

limitations: The camera counts each raise (your heel lifting above your toes); it does not judge technique beyond that. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view. Filmed from the front the heel is hidden and nothing is counted. Experimental.

name: Sumo Squat
purpose: Practise a wide-stance squat with the toes turned out and the chest tall.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Use a comfortable width and depth. Stop if you feel pain in your knees, hips or back.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than your shoulders and toes turned out.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Bend your knees and hips, letting the knees travel out over the toes.
Lower to a comfortable depth, then stand tall.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Push the knees gently out in line with your toes, or narrow your stance slightly.
Bring the feet a little closer or reduce the depth.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions and may suggest simple adjustments. Keep your whole body in view, facing the phone or side-on. Experimental.

name: Split Squat
purpose: Practise lowering and rising in a split stance without stepping, building single-leg control.
space: About 2 m front to back of clear floor, with a wall or chair within reach for balance.
safety: Keep a support within reach if your balance is unsure. Use a shallow depth to start. Stop if you feel pain in the knees or hips.
instructions: Take a long stride: one foot forward, the back foot on its ball.
Keep your feet hip-width apart side to side.
Lower straight down until the back knee is a hand's width above the floor, or as low as is comfortable.
Rise back up; finish all reps, then switch legs.
commonCues: Front knee over the middle of the foot.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lengthen your stance a little.
Keep a little width between the feet for balance.

limitations: The camera counts each repetition and, side-on, can suggest keeping your chest tall. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Side Lunge
purpose: Practise shifting your weight over one leg to the side while the other leg stays long.
space: About 2.5 m side to side of clear, non-slip floor.
safety: Move within a comfortable range and keep the bent knee in line with the toes. Stop if you feel pain in the knees, hips or groin.
instructions: Stand with your feet wide apart, toes turned out slightly.
Shift your hips back and over one foot, bending that knee.
Keep the other leg long with the foot flat.
Push back to the middle, then go to the other side.

commonMistakes.mistake: Knee drifting past the toes and inward
commonMistakes.adjustment: Send the hips further back and keep the knee over the foot.
Keep the chest proud and reduce the depth.

limitations: The camera counts each side lunge from the bend of the working knee. Face the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Knee Push-up
purpose: Practise the push-up pattern from the knees, keeping one straight line from knees to head.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Use a soft surface under the knees. Lower only as far as you can control. Stop if you feel pain in your wrists, shoulders or back.
instructions: Kneel and place your hands on the floor a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from knees to head.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
commonCues: Straight line from knees to head.
Elbows angle back, not straight out.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring the hips down into line with the shoulders and knees.
Angle the elbows back about 45 degrees from the body.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions and can suggest keeping your hips in line. Turn the phone sideways and place it on the floor side-on or at an angle with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Slow Mountain Climber
purpose: Practise moving one leg at a time while holding a steady high plank.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Keep the pace slow and controlled. Rest whenever your plank position changes. Stop if you feel pain in the wrists, shoulders or back.
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Bring one knee toward your chest.
Return the foot to the plank.
Repeat with the other leg.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down and hold the plank still while the leg moves.
Pause in the plank between each knee drive.

limitations: The camera counts each knee drive (the knee coming in toward your chest from the plank); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Dead Bug
purpose: Practise moving opposite arm and leg while keeping your trunk still, lying on your back.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Move only as far as you can keep your lower back gently on the floor. Stop if you feel pain in your back or neck.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms pointing to the ceiling.
Lift your legs so hips and knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and straighten the opposite leg, stopping above the floor.
Return and switch sides.
commonCues: Lower back stays gently on the floor.
Move slowly; breathe out as you reach.

commonMistakes.mistake: Lower back arching off the floor
commonMistakes.adjustment: Make the movement smaller, or keep the knee bent as the leg reaches.
Breathe out as you reach, in as you return.

limitations: The camera counts each leg reach (the knee straightening as the leg reaches long); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Bird Dog
purpose: Practise reaching one arm forward and the opposite leg back while keeping your back steady on all fours.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Use a soft surface under the knees. Lift only to hip height. Stop if you feel pain in your back, wrists or knees.
instructions: Kneel on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are about level with your body.
Hold briefly, keeping the back flat and the hips level.
Return and switch sides.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift the leg a little lower and keep both hip bones pointing at the floor.
Reach long instead of high.

limitations: The camera counts each reach (the back leg straightening); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Superman
purpose: Practise lifting the arms, chest and legs a few centimetres while lying face down.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Lift only a small, comfortable amount and keep your neck long. Stop if you feel pain in your back or neck.
instructions: Lie face down with your arms reaching forward.
Gently lift your arms, chest and legs a few centimetres off the floor.
Hold for a breath, looking at the floor.
Lower slowly.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep looking at the floor just in front of you.
A few centimetres is enough.

limitations: The camera counts each lift (your feet lifting off the floor); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. A person lying face down can take the camera a moment to find. Experimental.

name: High-Knee March
purpose: A brisk march lifting the knees toward hip height to raise the heart rate without jumping.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Keep a pace you can talk at. Stop if you feel dizzy, short of breath or unwell.
instructions: Stand tall.
Lift one knee toward hip height while the opposite arm swings forward.
Place the foot down softly and switch.
Keep a steady rhythm.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning back to lift the knee
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift a little lower and keep your chest over your hips.

limitations: The camera counts each knee lift from how high your knee rises; it does not judge technique. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Standing Knee Crunch
purpose: Lift one knee at a time while gently curling the upper body toward it, for core control without lying down.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Move slowly and keep your balance; stand near a wall if you feel unsteady. Do not pull on your head or neck. Stop if you feel pain in your back or hips.
instructions: Stand tall with your fingertips lightly at the sides of your head, elbows wide.
Lift one knee toward hip height while you curl your chest a little toward it.
Lower the foot softly and stand tall again.
Switch sides and keep a steady rhythm.

commonMistakes.mistake: Pulling the head forward with the hands
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the fingertips light; the movement comes from your middle.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning back to lift the knee
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift the knee a little lower and keep your chest over your hips.

limitations: The camera counts each knee lift from how high your knee rises; it does not judge technique. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Arm Circles
purpose: A shoulder warm-up: small circles with the arms out to the sides, forward then backward.
space: Room to reach both arms out to the sides.
safety: Keep the circles small and comfortable. Stop if you feel pain in your shoulders.
instructions: Stand tall and raise your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Make small forward circles.
Switch to small backward circles.
Lower the arms to rest.
commonCues: Shoulders down, away from the ears.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Relax the shoulders down while the arms circle.

limitations: The camera times your hold only while you're in the position (both arms out at shoulder height); it does not judge effort or how long you should hold. Face the phone with your upper body and both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Cat-Cow
purpose: A gentle spine mobility drill on all fours: round the back, then let the chest sink.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Move slowly within a comfortable range. Stop if you feel pain in your back or neck.
instructions: Kneel on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Round your back toward the ceiling and let your head drop (cat).
Let your chest sink and lift your gaze slightly (cow).
Move slowly between the two with your breath.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Make the movement smaller and smoother.

limitations: The camera counts each round (your head lowering and lifting with your back); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
purpose: Practise curling light dumbbells with the elbows staying by your sides.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Start with a light weight you can lift with control. Stop if you feel pain in your elbows, wrists or back.
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides, palms forward.
Keep your elbows by your sides.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Use a lighter weight and keep the torso still.
Pin the elbows to your sides.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how high your hands rise; it does not judge technique. Keep your upper body and arms in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
purpose: Practise curling light dumbbells with the palms facing each other.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Start with a light weight you can lift with control. Stop if you feel pain in your elbows, wrists or back.
instructions: Stand tall with the dumbbells by your sides, palms facing in.
Keep the elbows by your sides and curl the weights up, thumbs leading.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly all the way.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Use a lighter weight and keep your torso still.
Keep the elbows close to your ribs.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how high your hands rise; it does not judge technique. Keep your upper body and arms in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
purpose: Practise pressing light dumbbells from shoulder height to overhead.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor. Room to reach overhead.
safety: Use a light weight and keep your ribs down. Stop if you feel pain in your shoulders, neck or back.
instructions: Stand tall with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Brace gently and keep your ribs down.
Press the weights straight up until the arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly back to the shoulders.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Use a lighter weight and keep the ribs down.
Finish with the weights over your shoulders, not in front.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how high your hands rise; it does not judge technique. Keep your upper body and arms in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
purpose: Practise raising light dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Use a very light weight. Raise only to shoulder height. Stop if you feel pain in your shoulders.
instructions: Stand tall with dumbbells by your sides and a soft bend in the elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Use a lighter weight and keep the shoulders down.
Slow down and pause at the bottom.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how high your hands rise; it does not judge technique. Keep your upper body and arms in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
purpose: Practise raising light dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Use a very light weight. Raise only to shoulder height. Stop if you feel pain in your shoulders or back.
instructions: Stand tall with the dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Raise your arms in front of you to shoulder height with a soft bend in the elbows.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning back to lift the weight
commonMistakes.adjustment: Use a lighter weight and keep your torso still.
Stop when your hands reach shoulder height.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how high your hands rise; it does not judge technique. Keep your upper body and arms in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension
purpose: Practise bending and straightening the elbows overhead to work the back of the arms.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor. Clear space above your head.
safety: Use a very light weight and move slowly so the weights never touch your head. Stop if you feel pain in your elbows, shoulders or back.
instructions: Stand tall and press light dumbbells straight overhead.
Keep your upper arms beside your ears.
Bend the elbows slowly to lower the weights behind your head.
Straighten the arms to press back up.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the upper arms close to your head.
Brace your middle and use a lighter weight.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how far your hands drop and rise; it does not judge technique. Keep your upper body and arms in view, with your hands visible overhead. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Bent-over Row
purpose: Practise pulling light dumbbells toward your ribs while holding a flat-back hip hinge.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Learn the hip hinge first. Keep your back flat and the weight light. Stop if you feel pain in your back.
instructions: Hold dumbbells and hinge at the hips with soft knees until your body leans forward about 45 degrees.
Let the arms hang straight down.
Pull the elbows back past your ribs.
Lower the weights slowly.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Hinge less far and use a lighter weight.
Slow the pull and pause at the top.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions while you stay hinged; it does not judge technique. Keep your whole body in view, side-on or at an angle. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
purpose: Practise the hip hinge holding light dumbbells close to your legs.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Learn the bodyweight hip hinge first. Lower only as far as your back stays flat. Stop if you feel pain in your back or hamstrings.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Soften your knees and push your hips back.
Slide the weights down close to your legs, keeping your back flat.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall.
commonCues: Weights stay close to the legs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach lower
commonMistakes.adjustment: Stop higher, where your back is still flat.

commonMistakes.mistake: Bending the knees into a squat
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the shins nearly vertical and move from the hips.

limitations: The camera counts each repetition from how far your upper body tips forward; it does not judge your back position. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
purpose: Practise lifting a kettlebell from between your feet with a flat back and a strong hip drive.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Use a light kettlebell and keep it close. Keep your back flat throughout. Stop if you feel pain in your back.
instructions: Stand with feet wider than hip-width, the kettlebell between your feet.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to grip the handle with both hands.
Brace and stand up by driving through your feet, keeping your back flat.
Lower the kettlebell back down the same way.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Bend the knees a little more and keep the chest proud.
Finish standing straight, squeezing the glutes.

limitations: The camera counts each repetition from how far your upper body tips forward; it does not judge your back position. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Band Pull-apart
purpose: Practise pulling a light resistance band apart in front of you to work the upper back.
space: Room to reach both arms out to the sides.
safety: Check the band for nicks or tears before use and keep it away from your face. Use a light band. Stop if you feel pain in your shoulders.
instructions: Hold a light band in front of you at shoulder height, arms straight, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull your hands apart until your arms are out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly.
Return slowly.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears.
Keep the ribs down.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how far your hands move apart. Face the phone with your upper body and arms in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
purpose: Practise opening the arms out to the sides from a hip hinge to work the upper back and rear shoulders.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Learn the hip hinge first. Use a very light weight and keep your back flat. Stop if you feel pain in your back or shoulders.
instructions: Hold light dumbbells and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and soft knees.
Let the weights hang under your shoulders, elbows softly bent.
Open your arms out to the sides until they are about level with your back.
Lower slowly under control.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Use a lighter weight and pause at the top.
Hinge a little less and keep your chest proud.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from how far your hands travel; it does not judge technique. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Incline Push-up
purpose: Practise the push-up with your hands on a sturdy raised surface, which makes it easier.
space: A sturdy bench, table or kitchen counter that will not slide, with clear floor behind it.
safety: Make sure the surface is stable and will not move or tip. Lower only as far as you can control. Stop if you feel pain in your wrists, shoulders or back.
instructions: Place your hands on the edge of a sturdy surface a little wider than your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body forms a straight line.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the edge.
Press back up.
commonCues: Straight line from head to heels.
The higher the surface, the easier it is.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Squeeze your glutes, or use a higher surface.
Use something that cannot slide or tip, such as a counter.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions and can suggest keeping your hips in line. Keep your whole body and the bench in view, side-on or at an angle. Experimental.

name: Boxing Stance
purpose: Learn a balanced, relaxed starting position used in beginner boxing practice.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear floor. Wear supportive footwear or train on a non-slip surface.
safety: Practise without contact. Keep enough clear space around you. Learn martial arts technique from a qualified instructor.
instructions: Stand in a comfortable staggered stance.
Keep knees relaxed rather than locked.
Bring hands to a comfortable guard position.
Practise returning to a balanced neutral position.
commonCues: Make sure your full body is visible.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Step the feet roughly hip-width apart so you feel stable when shifting your weight.
Keep a slight, relaxed bend in both knees.
Hold the hands near the face in a relaxed guard without squeezing.

limitations: This is a beginner educational guide, not a certification of boxing technique.

name: Jab
purpose: Practise the lead-hand extension slowly, focusing on balance and returning to guard.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly in open space without hitting people or objects. Stop if uncomfortable.
instructions: Begin from a comfortable boxing stance.
Practise a slow, controlled lead-hand extension.
Return the hand to guard.
Reset your balance before repeating.
commonCues: Do not chase speed or power.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the rear hand near your face while the lead hand extends.
Extend smoothly and stop just short of a fully locked elbow.
Stay balanced over your feet; it is fine if the hand does not travel far.

limitations: Do not estimate impact, force, combat effectiveness, or injury risk.

name: Cross
purpose: Practise the rear-hand extension slowly with a controlled turn of the body.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Begin from a comfortable stance.
Watch the 3D demonstration from more than one angle.
Practise a slow, controlled movement.
Return to a balanced stance.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Make the movement smaller and slower until you feel stable.
Bring the hand straight back to your face before the next repetition.
Turn only as far as feels comfortable for your hips and back.

limitations: The camera counts crosses and checks that the lead hand stays up and the punch comes back to guard. It does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Experimental.

name: Jab-Cross (1-2)
purpose: Practise linking the jab and the cross into the basic one-two combination.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Throw the jab and bring it back.
As the jab returns, throw the cross, turning the rear hip and heel.
Return both hands to guard and reset.
commonCues: Jab back as the cross goes.
Turn the rear hip and heel.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping the lead hand during the cross
commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring the jab all the way back to your face first.
Slow down until both punches are clean.

limitations: The camera counts each one-two combination; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Throw the two punches as one flowing combination, facing the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Jab-Cross-Hook (1-2-3)
purpose: Practise adding a lead hook to the one-two.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Throw the jab, then the cross.
As the cross returns, throw a lead hook: elbow up to shoulder height, turn from the lead foot and hips.
Return to guard and reset.
commonCues: Each punch starts as the last one comes home.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Throw it from where your hand is, turning the hips.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rear hand dropping during the hook
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the rear hand by your chin.

limitations: The camera counts each jab-cross-hook combination; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Throw the three punches as one flowing combination, facing the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Jab-Jab-Cross (1-1-2)
purpose: Practise the double jab followed by the cross.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Throw a jab, bring it back, and throw a second jab.
As the second jab returns, throw the cross, turning the rear hip and heel.
Return both hands to guard and reset.
commonCues: Rear hand stays on the chin during the jabs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping the lead hand after the jabs
commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring each jab all the way back to your face.

commonMistakes.mistake: Pushing the second jab out slowly
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep both jabs short and snappy.

limitations: The camera counts each 1-1-2 combination; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Throw the three punches as one flowing combination, facing the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Guard Return
purpose: Build the habit of bringing your hands back to a relaxed guard after each movement.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear floor. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise without contact and at a slow pace. Stop if uncomfortable.
instructions: Start in a comfortable boxing stance with hands in guard.
Let one hand move slightly away from the face.
Bring it straight back to guard.
Pause, check your balance, then repeat with the other hand.
commonCues: Return to the same guard position each time.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring the hand back up near the face before moving again.
Breathe out and let the shoulders relax.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Forward & Backward Footwork
purpose: Practise small, balanced steps forwards and backwards from your stance.
space: At least 3 m of clear, non-slip floor in front of and behind you.
safety: Use a clear, non-slip floor and small steps. Stop if you feel unsteady or uncomfortable.
instructions: Start in a comfortable boxing stance.
Step the front foot forward a short distance, then let the back foot follow.
Step the back foot backward a short distance, then let the front foot follow.
Keep the same stance width after each step.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the feet roughly hip-width apart and let the lead foot move first.
Shorten the step so you stay balanced.

limitations: Timer and instructions only. Footwork is not automatically scored.

name: Lead Hook
purpose: Practise the lead-hand hook slowly in the air: a short, bent-arm movement driven by turning the body.
space: Clear space around you of at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Shadowbox only; never strike people or objects. Practise slowly and turn only as far as is comfortable for your back and knees. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Begin from your boxing stance with your guard up.
Raise the lead elbow to about shoulder height with the arm bent and the forearm level.
Turn your lead foot, hips and shoulders together so the fist travels around in front of your chin.
Return straight to guard.
commonCues: Turn the body, not just the arm.
Keep the rear hand by your face.
Short and controlled; back to guard.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the elbow bent and the movement short, close to your body.

commonMistakes.mistake: Twisting on a planted lead foot
commonMistakes.adjustment: Let the lead heel turn out so the knee stays comfortable.
Keep the rear fist next to your face throughout.

limitations: The camera counts each hook from your elbow coming up to shoulder height; it does not judge power or technique. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Slip
purpose: Practise moving your head a short distance off the centre line with a small bend of the knees and body, then returning.
space: Clear space around you of at least an arm's length. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Solo practice only; never practise with someone throwing punches at you. Keep the movement small and slow. Stop if you feel dizzy or have pain in your back or neck.
instructions: Begin from your boxing stance with your guard up.
Bend your knees slightly and lean your upper body a short way to one side, moving your head just off the centre line.
Return to centre.
Repeat to the other side.
commonCues: Bend the knees; don't bend over at the waist.
Hands stay up by your face.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Move only far enough to take your head just off the centre line.
Keep your eyes forward throughout.
Keep both fists by your face as you move.

limitations: The camera counts each slip from your head moving off the centre line and back. Face the phone with your head and upper body in view. Experimental.

name: Side-to-Side Footwork
purpose: Practise stepping sideways in your stance with short push-steps, keeping the same stance width.
space: About 2 m side to side of clear, non-slip floor.
safety: Keep steps short and the floor clear. Stop if you feel unsteady or have pain in your knees or ankles.
instructions: Begin from your boxing stance with your guard up.
To move left, step the left foot first, then follow with the right.
To move right, step the right foot first, then follow with the left.
Keep the same stance width after every step.
commonCues: The foot nearest the direction moves first.
Short steps; never cross your feet.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Step with the foot nearest the direction of travel first, then follow.

commonMistakes.mistake: Feet ending up too close together
commonMistakes.adjustment: Check your stance width after every step.
Stay level and glide with short steps.

limitations: This is a guided drill. The camera does not score footwork.

name: Rear Uppercut
purpose: Practise the rear-hand uppercut slowly in the air: a short upward punch driven by the legs and hips.
space: Clear space around you of at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Shadowbox only; never strike people or objects. Practise slowly. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Begin from your boxing stance with your guard up.
Dip slightly by bending your knees.
Drive up from the legs and turn the hips as the rear fist rises close to your body to chin height, palm toward you.
Return straight to guard.
commonCues: Short and close to the body.
Lead hand stays by your face.

commonMistakes.mistake: Winding up by dropping the hand low
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the drop small; the power comes from the legs.
Keep the lead fist by your face.

limitations: The camera counts each uppercut from your elbow driving up; it does not judge power or technique. Face the phone with both arms in view — turned away, the rear arm is hidden. Experimental.

name: Lead Uppercut
purpose: Practise the lead-hand uppercut slowly in the air.
space: Clear space around you of at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Shadowbox only; never strike people or objects. Practise slowly. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Begin from your boxing stance with your guard up.
Bend the knees slightly and shift a little weight to the lead side.
Drive up as the lead fist rises close to your body to chin height, palm toward you.
Return straight to guard.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Stay balanced over your feet.
Keep the fist close and rising straight up.

limitations: The camera counts each uppercut from your elbow driving up; it does not judge power or technique. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Rear Hook
purpose: Practise the rear-hand hook slowly in the air, turning the body through with the rear foot.
space: Clear space around you of at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Shadowbox only; never strike people or objects. Practise slowly and turn only as far as is comfortable. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Begin from your boxing stance with your guard up.
Pivot on the ball of the rear foot and turn your hips and shoulders.
The rear elbow rises to about shoulder height and the fist swings round in front of your chin.
Return straight to guard.
commonCues: Turn the body, not just the arm.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the movement short and close.

commonMistakes.mistake: Twisting on a flat rear foot
commonMistakes.adjustment: Let the rear heel lift and turn.

limitations: The camera counts each hook from your elbow coming up to shoulder height; it does not judge power or technique. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Roll
purpose: Practise moving your head under an imaginary punch with a small U-shaped bend of the knees.
space: Clear space around you of at least an arm's length. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Solo practice only; never practise with someone throwing punches at you. Bend at the knees, not the waist, and keep the movement small. Stop if you feel dizzy or have pain in your back or knees.
instructions: Begin from your boxing stance with your guard up.
Bend your knees and move your upper body in a small U shape from one side to the other.
Rise up on the other side.
Return and repeat the other way.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Use the knees and keep the chest more upright.
Keep your eyes forward.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments, and counts each roll from your shoulders dipping and coming back up; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Pivot
purpose: Practise turning your stance on the ball of the lead foot to change angle.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, non-slip floor.
safety: Keep the turn small and the floor clear. Stop if you feel unsteady or have pain in your knees or ankles.
instructions: Begin from your boxing stance with your guard up.
Stay on the ball of the lead foot.
Swing the rear foot around so the whole stance turns a little.
Turn back and reset your stance.
commonCues: Pivot on the ball of the lead foot.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift the lead heel slightly and turn on the ball.
Check your stance after each pivot.

limitations: This is a guided drill. The camera does not score footwork.

name: Dumbbell Squat
purpose: Add light load to the bodyweight squat with a dumbbell held at each side.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Master the bodyweight squat first. Use a light weight you can control for every rep. Stop if you feel pain in your knees, hips or back.
instructions: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, arms long at your sides, palms facing in.
Sit your hips back and down, knees following the direction of your toes.
Keep your chest up and let the weights hang straight down.
Push through the whole foot to stand tall.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Sit back a little more and go only as low as your heels stay down.
Let the arms hang; the legs do the work.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from your knee angle; it does not judge technique or the load. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
purpose: The reverse lunge with a light dumbbell in each hand, alternating legs.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor, with room to step back.
safety: Learn the bodyweight reverse lunge first. Use light weights and step back only as far as you can control. Stop if you feel pain in your knees or hips.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms long at your sides.
Step one foot back and lower until the back knee is a hand's width above the floor.
Keep the front knee over the middle of the foot and the chest tall.
Push through the front foot to step back to standing, then switch legs.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down and keep the arms relaxed and long.
Keep the knee pointing over the middle toes; take a shorter step.

limitations: The camera counts each lunge from how far your hips lower; it does not judge technique or the load. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Standing Oblique Crunch
purpose: Lift one knee out to the side while bending sideways toward it, for the sides of your core without lying down.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Move slowly and keep your balance; stand near a wall if you feel unsteady. Do not pull on your head or neck. Stop if you feel pain in your back or hips.
instructions: Stand tall with your fingertips lightly at the sides of your head, elbows wide.
Lift one knee up and out to the side.
At the same time bend sideways so that elbow comes down toward the knee.
Lower the foot, stand tall, and switch sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Twisting forward instead of bending sideways
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the chest facing forward and shorten the side of your waist.

commonMistakes.mistake: Pulling the head down with the hand
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the fingertips light; the elbow follows your side.

limitations: The camera counts each knee lift from how high your knee rises; it does not judge technique. Face the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Double Jab
purpose: Practise two quick jabs in a row, bringing the hand back to the face between them.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Throw a jab and bring it back toward your face.
As it comes back, throw the second jab.
Return the hand to guard and reset before the next pair.
commonCues: Rear hand stays on the chin.
Don't lean in on the second jab.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring it back at least to chin level before the second.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning forward on the second jab
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep your head over your stance; reach with the arm, not the body.

limitations: The camera counts each double jab as one; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Jab to the Body
purpose: Practise changing level with your legs and jabbing to body height, then coming back up into your stance.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing. Bend your knees to lower yourself; stop if you feel pain in your knees or back.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Bend your knees to lower your body a little; keep your back straight, don't bend at the waist.
Jab straight out at chest height of an imaginary opponent, rear hand on your chin.
Bring the hand back to your face and stand back up into your stance.
commonCues: Legs take you down, not your back.
Back up to your stance after every punch.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lower yourself with the knees and keep your chest up.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping the rear hand as you go down
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the rear glove touching your chin.

limitations: The camera counts each time you lower and come back up; a jab thrown straight at the phone is hard to see, so the punch itself is not checked. Keep your whole body, feet included, in view. Experimental.

name: Cross-Hook (2-3)
purpose: Practise the cross followed by the lead hook, turning the hips one way and then the other.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Throw the cross, turning your rear hip and pivoting on the rear foot.
As the cross comes back, turn the hips the other way and throw the lead hook, elbow up at shoulder height.
Return both hands to guard and reset.
commonCues: Hook elbow level with the fist.

commonMistakes.mistake: Swinging the hook wide with a straight arm
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the elbow bent about 90 degrees and turn your body to bring it round.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the cross out while the hook starts
commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring the cross back to your chin first.

limitations: The camera counts each cross-hook as one combination; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Pull Back
purpose: Practise leaning back just out of reach of a straight punch while keeping your hands up and eyes forward.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing. Lean back only a little; stop if you feel pain in your lower back.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Shift your weight onto your rear leg and lean your upper body back a little.
Keep your chin down and your eyes forward, hands by your face.
Come forward again into your stance.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning back too far and losing balance
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lean only until your shoulders are just behind your hips.

commonMistakes.mistake: Lifting the chin and looking at the ceiling
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the chin tucked and look at your target.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments, and counts each pull-back from your head moving back off its line (best from a front corner); it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Step Jab
purpose: Practise jabbing as you take a small step forward, then stepping back out.
space: Clear space in front of you of at least two steps plus an arm's length. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Push off the rear foot and step the lead foot forward a short distance.
Land the jab as the lead foot lands; the rear foot follows to keep your stance width.
Step back the same way, rear foot first, hands in guard.
commonCues: Jab lands with the front foot.
Step back out after the jab.

commonMistakes.mistake: Throwing the jab after the step has finished
commonMistakes.adjustment: Start the jab as the lead foot leaves the floor.
Keep the same distance between your feet before and after the step.

limitations: The camera counts each jab from your elbow rising; it does not judge the step, power or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Good Morning (Bodyweight)
purpose: Practise the hip hinge with the arms folded: the hips go back while the back stays long.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Keep the movement small and slow. Stop if you feel pain in your lower back or hamstrings.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, arms folded across your chest.
Push your hips back and let your chest tip forward with a long, flat back.
Stop when you feel a stretch behind the thighs, about halfway down.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the chest open and stop the hinge a little higher.

commonMistakes.mistake: Bending the knees into a squat
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the knees only slightly bent and send the hips back.

limitations: The camera counts each hinge (your chest tipping forward and coming back up); it does not judge technique beyond that. Side-on or at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Curtsy Lunge
purpose: Lunge with the back leg crossing behind, for the legs, hips and balance.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Use a small step at first and keep the front knee over the toes. Stop if you feel pain in your knees or hips.
instructions: Stand tall, hands together in front of your chest.
Step one foot back and across behind the other, landing on the ball of the foot.
Bend both knees and lower with control, front knee over the toes.
Push through the front foot to stand and bring the feet together. Switch sides.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Take a smaller step across and keep the knee in line with the toes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Twisting the hips a long way
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the hips mostly facing forward.

limitations: The camera counts each lunge from your hip height when you stand tall; it does not judge technique. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Squat to Calf Raise
purpose: A squat followed by a rise onto the toes, for the legs and ankles.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Rise onto the toes only once you are standing still. Stop if you feel pain in your knees or ankles.
instructions: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, hands together at the chest.
Squat down with control, chest tall, knees over the toes.
Stand up fully.
Rise onto the balls of the feet, pause, and lower the heels slowly.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rising onto the toes while still in the squat
commonMistakes.adjustment: Stand up fully first, then rise.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling onto the outside of the feet
commonMistakes.adjustment: Press through the big toes as you rise.

limitations: The camera counts each squat (your knees bending and straightening); it does not judge technique beyond that. Keep your whole body in view, side-on or facing the phone. Experimental.

name: Single-Leg Balance
purpose: Balance on one leg with the other knee lifted, for ankle and hip control.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Stand next to a wall or chair you can touch. Stop if you feel unsteady or feel pain.
instructions: Stand tall with your arms relaxed slightly away from your sides.
Shift your weight onto one foot.
Lift the other knee in front of you and hold, breathing steadily.
Lower the foot with control and switch sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning the trunk to one side
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the shoulders level over the hips.
Keep a tiny bend in the standing knee.

limitations: The camera times your hold only while you're in the position (one foot clearly off the floor); it does not judge effort or how long you should hold. Face the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
purpose: A one-leg hip hinge without weights, for balance and the back of the legs.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Go only as far as you can keep your balance and a long back. Stop if you feel pain in your back or hamstrings.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the knee soft.
Hinge forward from the hip while the other leg reaches back in line with your body.
Let the arms hang toward the floor; keep the hips level.
Return to standing with control. Switch sides.
commonCues: Body and back leg move as one.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Point the toes of the back leg toward the floor.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach lower
commonMistakes.adjustment: Stop higher, with the back long.

limitations: The camera counts each hinge (your chest tipping forward and coming back up); it does not judge technique beyond that. Side-on or at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Standing Side Leg Raise
purpose: Lift the leg out to the side, for the outer hips and balance.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Hold a chair or wall if you need to. Stop if you feel pain in your hips or lower back.
instructions: Stand tall with your weight on one leg.
Lift the other leg out to the side, toes facing forward.
Raise it only as high as you can keep the trunk upright.
Lower with control. Switch sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning far over to lift higher
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift lower and keep the trunk tall.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning the toes up to the ceiling
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the toes pointing forward.

limitations: The camera counts each raise (the working leg swinging out from vertical); it does not judge technique beyond that. Face the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Standing Glute Kickback
purpose: Sweep the straight leg back from the hip, for the glutes.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Keep the movement small and the lower back still. Stop if you feel pain in your lower back.
instructions: Stand tall, leaning a little forward, with your weight on one leg.
Sweep the other leg straight back from the hip.
Stop before your lower back arches.
Bring the leg back with control. Switch sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back to kick higher
commonMistakes.adjustment: Make the movement smaller.
Move slowly and pause at the back.

limitations: The camera counts each kickback (the working leg swinging back from vertical); it does not judge technique beyond that. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Low-Impact Butt Kicks
purpose: Walk on the spot bringing each heel toward the seat, to warm up.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Keep it low-impact: one foot stays on the floor. Stop if you feel pain in your knees.
instructions: Stand tall with the arms bent at your sides.
Lift one heel behind you toward your seat, the knee pointing down.
Put it down and lift the other heel.
Keep a steady rhythm and swing the arms.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Stay tall through the chest.
Keep the thigh pointing down; only the heel lifts.

limitations: The camera counts each kick (the heel rising up behind toward the knee); it does not judge technique beyond that. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Standing Torso Twist
purpose: A gentle turning warm-up for the upper back.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Turn only as far as is comfortable, slowly. Stop if you feel pain in your back.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, arms bent in front of your chest.
Turn your chest and head to one side while the hips stay mostly facing forward.
Come back through the middle and turn to the other side.
Keep the movement smooth.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down and control the turn.
Let the hips stay mostly still.

limitations: The camera counts each twist (your hands, together at your chest, turning to each side); it does not judge technique beyond that. Face the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Standing Side Bend
purpose: Reach up and over, to stretch the sides of the body.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Bend only as far as is comfortable. Stop if you feel pain in your back or neck.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Reach one arm up and over toward the other side.
Let the other hand slide down the outside of the thigh.
Come back up slowly and switch sides.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the chest facing forward and bend sideways.
Reach up and over rather than down.

limitations: The camera counts each bend (your shoulders leaning to the side over your hips); it does not judge technique beyond that. Face the phone with your upper body in view. Experimental.

name: Low-Impact Skater
purpose: Step side to side with the back foot sweeping behind, for the legs and balance.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Keep one foot on the floor at all times. Stop if you feel pain in your knees or ankles.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the knee bent and the chest a little forward.
Step wide to the other side and land softly on that foot.
Let the other foot sweep behind and touch lightly with the toes.
Swing the arms and repeat to the other side.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Bend the knee as you land.
Keep the knee in line with the toes.

limitations: The camera counts each skate (your hips travelling side to side); it does not judge technique beyond that. Face the phone with your whole body in view. Leave room to step. Experimental.

name: Wall Push-up
purpose: An easier push-up against a wall, for the chest, shoulders and arms.
space: A clear wall with space to stand an arm's length away.
safety: Make sure your feet will not slip. Stop if you feel pain in your shoulders or wrists.
instructions: Stand facing a wall, a little more than an arm's length away.
Put your hands on the wall at shoulder height, a little wider than the shoulders.
Keep the body in one straight line and bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall.
Press back to the start.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Tighten the stomach and glutes.
Bring the elbows a little closer to the body.

limitations: The camera counts each rep (your elbows bending and straightening); it does not judge technique beyond that. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Wall Sit
purpose: Hold a seated position against a wall, for the thighs.
space: A clear, smooth wall and non-slip floor.
safety: Go only as low as is comfortable for your knees. Stop if you feel pain in your knees.
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a wall, feet out in front.
Slide down until your thighs are a little above level and the knees are over the ankles.
Rest the hands on the thighs and hold, breathing steadily.
Slide back up the wall to stand.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Walk the feet further from the wall.
Breathe slowly and evenly.

limitations: The camera times your hold only while you're in the position (back upright, knees bent), and may suggest sliding a little lower toward a right angle; it does not judge effort or how long you should hold. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Goblet Squat
purpose: A squat holding one dumbbell upright at the chest.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Master the bodyweight squat first. Use a light weight you can control for every rep. Stop if you feel pain in your knees, hips or back.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell upright against your chest, both hands cupping the top end.
Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Squat down with control, elbows inside the knees, chest tall.
Stand up by pushing through the whole foot.

commonMistakes.mistake: Letting the weight pull you forward
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep it tight against the chest.
Squat a little less deep and sit back.

limitations: The camera counts repetitions from your knee angle; it does not judge technique or the load. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
purpose: A chest press lying on the floor, for the chest, shoulders and arms.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Use light weights you can control. Lower slowly until the upper arms touch the floor. Stop if you feel pain in your shoulders.
instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, a dumbbell in each hand.
Upper arms on the floor at about 45 degrees from the body, forearms pointing up.
Press the dumbbells up over the chest.
Lower slowly until the upper arms touch the floor again.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping the weights onto the floor
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lower slowly and let the elbows touch softly.
Keep them at about 45 degrees.

limitations: The camera counts each press (your hands pressing up from your shoulders); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
purpose: Lift the shoulders straight up, for the upper back and neck muscles.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Use light weights and move only the shoulders. Stop if you feel pain in your neck.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms long at your sides.
Lift the shoulders straight up toward the ears.
Pause briefly.
Lower the shoulders slowly.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Move straight up and down only.
Keep the arms long and let the shoulders do the work.

limitations: The camera counts each shrug (your shoulders lifting toward your ears); it does not judge technique beyond that. Face the phone with your head and shoulders in view. Experimental.

name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
purpose: Rise onto the toes holding dumbbells, for the calves.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Master the bodyweight calf raise first. Stop if you feel pain in your feet, ankles or calves.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Rise onto the balls of the feet.
Pause at the top.
Lower the heels slowly to the floor.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling onto the outside of the feet
commonMistakes.adjustment: Press through the big toes.
Lower slowly and pause at the bottom.

limitations: The camera counts each raise (your heel lifting above your toes); it does not judge technique beyond that. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view. Filmed from the front the heel is hidden and nothing is counted. Experimental.

name: Kettlebell Swing
purpose: A two-hand swing driven by the hips, for the glutes, hamstrings and back.
space: About 2 × 3 m of clear floor, nothing in front or behind you.
safety: Learn the hip hinge first and use a light kettlebell. Keep everyone clear of the swing. Stop if you feel pain in your back.
instructions: Stand with feet a little wider than the hips, the kettlebell held in both hands.
Hinge back so the bell swings back between the thighs.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall; let the straight arms float to chest height.
Let the bell fall back into the next hinge. Finish by standing still.

commonMistakes.mistake: Lifting the bell with the arms
commonMistakes.adjustment: Let the hip drive do the work; the arms only guide.
Send the hips back with a soft knee.

limitations: The camera counts each swing (your hips folding and snapping open); it does not judge technique beyond that. Side-on or at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Bench Dip (Bent Knees)
purpose: Lower and press the body with the hands on a bench behind you, for the triceps.
space: A sturdy bench or chair that will not slide.
safety: Use a stable bench that will not slide. Lower only until the elbows are about 90 degrees. Stop if you feel pain in your shoulders or wrists.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands on the edge beside your hips, fingers forward.
Walk the feet forward with the knees bent and slide the hips just off the bench.
Bend the elbows to lower the hips, shoulders down away from the ears.
Press back up.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Stop when the elbows reach about 90 degrees.
Keep them pressed down.

limitations: The camera counts each dip (your elbows bending and straightening); it does not judge technique beyond that. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Crunch
purpose: Curl the head and shoulders off the floor, for the stomach muscles.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Keep the lower back on the floor and the neck relaxed. Stop if you feel pain in your neck or back.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, arms folded on the chest.
Curl the head and shoulders a little off the floor.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the arms folded on the chest.
Lift only the head and shoulders.

limitations: The camera counts each crunch (your shoulders curling up off the floor); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Heel Taps
purpose: Reach side to side toward the heels, for the sides of the stomach.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Keep the neck relaxed. Stop if you feel pain in your neck or back.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Lift the head and shoulders a little off the floor, arms long beside you.
Bend sideways to reach one hand toward that heel.
Come back through the middle and reach to the other side.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping the head to the floor between taps
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the shoulders lifted the whole set.
Look at the ceiling, chin slightly tucked.

limitations: The camera counts each tap (your hand reaching toward your heel); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Reverse Crunch
purpose: Curl the hips off the floor toward the chest, for the lower stomach muscles.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Move slowly without swinging the legs. Stop if you feel pain in your back.
instructions: Lie on your back, arms on the floor, legs in tabletop (hips and knees bent 90 degrees).
Curl the hips a little off the floor, bringing the knees toward the chest.
Pause briefly.
Lower the hips slowly back to the floor.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Make the movement smaller and slower.

commonMistakes.mistake: Pushing hard into the floor with the arms
commonMistakes.adjustment: Let the stomach do the work.

limitations: The camera counts each rep (your knees coming in toward your chest); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Tabletop Toe Taps
purpose: Lower one foot at a time to tap the floor, for stomach control.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Keep the lower back gently on the floor. Stop if you feel pain in your back.
instructions: Lie on your back, legs in tabletop.
Keep the knee bent and lower one foot from the hip until the toes touch the floor lightly.
Bring it back to tabletop.
Switch legs.

commonMistakes.mistake: The lower back arching off the floor
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lower the foot less far.
Lower slowly and with control.

limitations: The camera counts each tap (one foot lowering toward the floor); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: High Plank
purpose: Hold a straight line from head to heels on straight arms, for the trunk and shoulders.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Hold only as long as you can keep a straight line. Stop if you feel pain in your wrists, shoulders or back.
instructions: Put your hands under your shoulders and step the feet back.
Make one straight line from head to heels.
Keep the arms long with soft elbows.
Hold and breathe steadily.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Tighten the stomach and glutes.
Lower the hips into line.

limitations: The camera times your hold only while you're in the position (body long and level, hands under your shoulders), and may suggest lifting or lowering your hips into one line; it does not judge effort or how long you should hold. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Plank Shoulder Taps
purpose: Tap each shoulder from a high plank without letting the hips rock.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Widen the feet for balance. Stop if you feel pain in your wrists, shoulders or back.
instructions: Start in a high plank with the feet a little wider than the hips.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder.
Put the hand back where it was.
Switch hands, keeping the hips level.
commonCues: Hand back to the same spot.

commonMistakes.mistake: The hips rocking side to side
commonMistakes.adjustment: Widen the feet and slow down.
Keep one straight line.

limitations: The camera counts each tap (one hand lifting off the floor); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level at an angle (from a front corner), whole body in view; side-on the far hand is hidden and its taps are missed, head-on the legs are hidden and tracking pauses. Experimental.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
purpose: A glute bridge on one leg, for the glutes and hamstrings.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Master the two-leg glute bridge first. Stop if you feel pain in your back or hamstrings.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Straighten one leg in line with the other thigh.
Lift the hips by pushing through the planted heel.
Lower with control. Switch sides.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift less high and keep the hips level.

commonMistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back at the top
commonMistakes.adjustment: Stop when shoulders, hips and knee are in line.

limitations: The camera counts each lift (your hips rising); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Quadruped Glute Kickback
purpose: On all fours, lift one bent leg back to hip height, for the glutes.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Keep the back flat and the movement slow. Stop if you feel pain in your back, wrists or knees.
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips.
Keep one knee bent at 90 degrees and lift that thigh back to hip height.
The sole of the foot faces the ceiling.
Lower with control. Switch sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Arching the back to lift higher
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift only to hip height.
Keep both hips facing the floor.

limitations: The camera counts each lift (the working knee moving away from the other knee); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level at an angle (from a front corner), whole body in view; side-on, the far leg is hidden and its lifts are missed. Experimental.

name: Fire Hydrant
purpose: On all fours, lift one bent knee out to the side, for the outer hips.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Keep the movement small and the back flat. Stop if you feel pain in your hips, back, wrists or knees.
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips.
Keep the knee bent and lift it out to the side.
Raise it only as high as you can without leaning.
Lower with control. Switch sides.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift less high and keep the shoulders level.
Pause at the top.

limitations: The camera counts each lift (the working knee moving away from the other knee); it does not judge technique beyond that. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level at a front corner on the side of the working leg, whole body in view; the leg further from the phone can be hidden behind the body and its lifts missed. Head-on, tracking fails on all fours. Experimental.

name: Child's Pose
purpose: A resting stretch for the back, hips and shoulders.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Widen the knees if the hips or knees feel tight. Stop if you feel pain in your knees.
instructions: Start on all fours.
Sit the hips back toward the heels.
Let the arms stay long on the floor and the forehead come toward the floor.
Breathe slowly, then come back to all fours.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Go only as far as is comfortable.
Breathe slowly into the back.

limitations: The camera times your hold only while you're in the position (hips back toward your heels, chest folded down); it does not judge effort or how long you should hold. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Bear Plank Hold
purpose: On all fours with the knees hovering just off the floor, for the trunk and shoulders.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
safety: Lift the knees only a few centimetres. Stop if you feel pain in your wrists, shoulders or back.
instructions: Start on all fours with the toes tucked.
Lift the knees a few centimetres off the floor.
Keep the back flat and the hips level.
Hold and breathe, then lower the knees.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the back flat, like a table.
Breathe slowly.

limitations: The camera times your hold only while you're in the position (on all fours, hands under the shoulders; the 2–3 cm knee hover itself is too small to see); it does not judge effort or how long you should hold. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Cross to the Body
purpose: Practise dropping your level with the knees and throwing the cross to the body.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
