safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Bend the knees to drop your level; keep the back straight.
Throw the cross to chest height of an imaginary opponent, turning the rear hip.
Come back up to your stance. Return both hands to guard and reset.
commonCues: Bend the knees, not the waist.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lower with the knees and keep the chest up.
Keep the lead glove by the cheek.

limitations: The camera counts each body shot when you come back up to your stance; it does not judge power or accuracy. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Lead Hook to the Body
purpose: Practise the lead hook to the body with a level change.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Bend the knees to drop your level.
Turn the lead hip and throw a short hook to the ribs, elbow bent.
Come back up. Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.mistake: Swinging wide with a straight arm
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the elbow bent and the punch short.
Stay centred between the feet.

limitations: The camera counts each body shot when you come back up to your stance; it does not judge power or accuracy. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Rear Hook to the Body
purpose: Practise the rear hook to the body, turned through by the rear foot and hips.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Bend the knees to drop your level.
Turn the rear hip and pivot the rear foot as the rear hook travels to the ribs.
Come back up. Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Let the body turn bring the hook round.
Keep it at the chin.

limitations: The camera counts each body shot when you come back up to your stance; it does not judge power or accuracy. Keep your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Jab, Cross to the Body
purpose: Combine a jab to the head with a cross to the body.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Jab to head height.
As it comes back, bend the knees and throw the cross to the body.
Come back up. Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.mistake: Bending at the waist for the body shot
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lower with the knees.
Bring it back before the cross.

limitations: The camera counts each combination when both hands are back in guard; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Jab Body-Head
purpose: Change levels with two jabs: the first to the body, the second to the head.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Bend the knees and jab to the body.
Come back up and jab to the head.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lower with the knees so the jab stays straight.
Keep it at the chin.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments, and counts each body-and-head pair from the jabbing elbow coming up and back to guard; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Parry
purpose: Practise tapping an imaginary jab aside with the rear hand.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Move the rear palm a short way across in front of your face.
Tap the imaginary jab aside, small and quick.
Return the hand straight to the chin.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the movement small, in front of your face.
Tap across, not down.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Catch
purpose: Practise catching an imaginary jab with the rear palm.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Open the rear palm a hand's width in front of your face.
Let the imaginary jab land in the palm; don't reach for it.
Return the hand to the chin.
commonCues: Palm in front of the face.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the hand close.
Keep the lead glove up.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: High Block (Cover)
purpose: Cover up with both gloves to the temples and the elbows in.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Bring both gloves up to the temples, forearms in front of the face.
Elbows down and in, chin tucked, knees soft.
Hold briefly, then return to guard.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep looking between the gloves.
Squeeze them in to protect the body.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Elbow Block (Body)
purpose: Drop the lead elbow to protect the ribs, with a small bend toward that side.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Drop the lead elbow onto the ribs, glove staying by the cheek.
Bend a little toward that side.
Return to guard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping the glove with the elbow
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the glove at the cheek.
Keep the bend small.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Duck
purpose: Lower under an imaginary punch by bending the knees.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Bend the knees to lower straight down, eyes forward.
Keep the hands up.
Come back up to your stance.

commonMistakes.mistake: Bending at the waist and looking down
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lower with the knees and keep the eyes forward.
Drop only a little below the imaginary punch.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments, and counts each duck from your shoulders dipping and coming back up; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Cover and Cross
purpose: Cover up, then answer with the cross.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Cover with both gloves to the temples.
As the gloves come down, throw the cross.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.mistake: Throwing the cross from the cover position
commonMistakes.adjustment: Return to guard first, then punch.
Keep it at the chin.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments, and counts each block-and-cross from the blocking elbow coming up and both hands back in guard; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Jab and Slip
purpose: Jab, then slip the head to the outside as the hand comes home.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Throw the jab.
As it returns, bend the knees a little and move the head to the right.
Come back to the middle.
commonCues: Bend the knees for the slip.

commonMistakes.mistake: Slipping before the jab is home
commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring the hand back first.
Move the head with a small bend.

limitations: The camera counts each slip when your head comes back to the middle; it does not judge timing. Face the phone with your head and upper body in view. Experimental.

name: Slip and Cross
purpose: Slip to the outside, then throw the cross as the head comes back.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Slip the head to the right with a small bend of the knees.
As the head comes back to the middle, throw the cross.
Return both hands to guard and reset.
commonCues: Head comes back through the middle.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Bring the head back to the middle first.
Keep it at the chin.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Roll and Hook
purpose: Roll under an imaginary hook, then answer with the lead hook.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Bend the knees and move the head in a U to the lead side.
As you come up on the lead side, throw the lead hook.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Make the U with the knees.
Keep the eyes forward.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments, and counts each roll-and-hook from the hooking elbow coming up and back to guard; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Pull Back and Cross
purpose: Lean back out of range, then come forward with the cross.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing. Lean back only a little; stop if you feel pain in your lower back.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Shift the weight onto the rear leg and lean the upper body back a little.
Come forward and throw the cross.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Lean only a little; stop if you feel pain in your lower back.
Keep both gloves up.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments, and counts each pull-and-counter from your head moving back off its line (best from a front corner); it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Jab-Rear Uppercut (1-6)
purpose: Combine a jab with the rear uppercut.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Throw the jab and bring it back.
Dip the knees and drive the rear uppercut up close to your body.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping the rear hand low before the uppercut
commonMistakes.adjustment: Only a small dip with the knees.
Keep the elbow close to the body.

limitations: The camera counts each combination when both hands are back in guard; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Lead Uppercut-Lead Hook (5-3)
purpose: Two punches off the lead hand: uppercut, then hook.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Throw the lead uppercut close to the body.
Turn the lead hip and throw the lead hook.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.mistake: Pulling the lead hand far back between punches
commonMistakes.adjustment: Go straight from one punch to the next.
Keep the elbow bent at about 90 degrees.

limitations: The camera counts each combination when both hands are back in guard; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Lead Hook-Cross (3-2)
purpose: The lead hook followed by the cross, turning the hips one way and back.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Throw the lead hook.
As it comes back, turn the rear hip and throw the cross.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the elbow bent.
Bring it back as the cross goes.

limitations: The camera counts each combination when both hands are back in guard; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Cross-Hook-Cross (2-3-2)
purpose: Three punches turning the hips back and forth: cross, lead hook, cross.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Throw the cross.
Throw the lead hook as the cross comes home.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Slow down and finish each punch.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep it at the chin.

name: Jab-Cross-Lead Uppercut (1-2-5)
purpose: The one-two finished with a lead uppercut.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Throw the jab and the cross.
As the cross comes back, dip slightly and throw the lead uppercut.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Only a small dip of the knees.
Bring it back as the uppercut starts.

limitations: The camera counts each combination when both hands are back in guard; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Lead and Rear Uppercut (5-6)
purpose: Two uppercuts, lead then rear, close to the body.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Throw the lead uppercut.
Turn the hips and throw the rear uppercut.
Return both hands to guard and reset.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the elbows close.
The hand not punching stays at the chin.

limitations: The camera counts each combination when both hands are back in guard; it does not judge power, speed or accuracy. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Stance Bounce
purpose: Light rhythm on the balls of the feet in your stance.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing. Keep it light; stop if you feel pain in your ankles or calves.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance, hands up.
Bounce lightly on the balls of the feet.
Keep the stance width the same.
Breathe steadily.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the bounce small.
Keep your stance width.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Fist Rolls
purpose: Roll the fists around each other in front of the chest, for shoulder endurance and rhythm.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Stand in your stance.
Bring the fists in front of the chest, forearms level.
Roll the fists around each other in small circles.
Keep a steady rhythm, then return to guard.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the circles small and close.
Relax the shoulders down.

limitations: The camera watches your guard (hands up by your face) and stance width and suggests simple adjustments; it does not judge timing, power or technique. Face the phone or stand at an angle, whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Circle Left
purpose: Move left with a push-step, then turn on the lead foot to face the target again.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Push-step to the left: the lead foot moves first, the rear foot follows.
Turn on the ball of the lead foot so you face the target again.
Return the same way.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Push-step; never cross.
Keep the feet as far apart as at the start.

limitations: The camera does not assess this movement in this version; follow the demonstration.

name: Circle Right
purpose: Move right with a push-step, then turn on the lead foot to face the target again.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Push-step to the right: the rear foot moves first, the lead foot follows.
Turn on the ball of the lead foot so you face the target again.
Return the same way.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Push-step; never cross.
Turn on the ball of the lead foot.

limitations: The camera does not assess this movement in this version; follow the demonstration.

name: Angle Step
purpose: Step forward and off the centre line, then turn to face the target.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Push-step forward and out to the left.
Turn on the lead foot to face the target again.
Step back the same way.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Step forward and out at an angle.
Keep both gloves up.

limitations: The camera does not assess this movement in this version; follow the demonstration.

name: In and Out
purpose: Quick, short push-steps forward and back, light on the feet.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Push-step forward a short distance.
Push-step straight back out.
Keep it light and repeat.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the steps short and quick.
Stay low and light.

limitations: The camera does not assess this movement in this version; follow the demonstration.

name: Jab Stepping Back
purpose: Jab as you push-step back out of range.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Push off the lead foot and step the rear foot back.
Jab as the lead foot follows.
Step back in to where you started.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Move the feet; keep the head over them.
Push-step and keep your stance width.

limitations: The camera counts each punch when the hand returns to guard; it does not judge power, speed, accuracy or footwork. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Side Step and Jab
purpose: Push-step to the left and jab as the lead foot lands.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Push-step to the left, lead foot first.
Jab as the lead foot lands.
Step back to the right, rear foot first.

commonMistakes.mistake: Jabbing before the feet are set
commonMistakes.adjustment: Land, then jab.
Push-step and keep your stance width.

limitations: The camera counts each punch when the hand returns to guard; it does not judge power, speed, accuracy or footwork. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Jab and Pivot
purpose: Jab, then pivot on the lead foot to take an angle.
space: Clear space in front of you at least an arm's length plus a step. Nothing and nobody within reach.
safety: Practise slowly without contact. Have a qualified coach review your technique before progressing.
instructions: Start in your boxing stance.
Throw the jab.
Pivot on the ball of the lead foot as the rear foot swings round.
Pivot back.
commonCues: Turn on the ball of the foot.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Turn on the ball of the lead foot.
Keep both gloves up.

limitations: The camera counts each punch when the hand returns to guard; it does not judge power, speed, accuracy or footwork. Face the phone with both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
purpose: Stretch the front of the thigh after training, while practising balance.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Stretch gently to a mild pull, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Hold a chair or wall if your balance is unsteady.
instructions: Stand tall on one leg, a hand on a chair or wall if you need it.
Bend the other knee and bring the heel up behind you toward your seat.
Hold the top of the foot with the same-side hand, knees side by side.
Hold for a few slow breaths, lower the foot, and switch sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Pulling the knee out to the side or forward
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the bent knee next to the standing knee, pointing down.
Tuck the hips under a little and stand tall.
Ease the heel up only until you feel a mild stretch.

limitations: The camera does not assess this stretch: seen by a phone, the folded leg behind the body is hidden and can't be measured reliably. Follow the demonstration; the timer guides the hold.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
purpose: Stretch the back of the shoulder after punching, pushing or pulling.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Stretch gently to a mild pull, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Keep the pressure light on the elbow.
instructions: Stand tall, shoulders relaxed down.
Bring one arm straight across the front of your chest at shoulder height.
Hook the other forearm just above the elbow and draw the arm in gently.
Hold for a few slow breaths, release, and switch sides.
commonCues: Press above the elbow, not on it.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Let the shoulder sink away from your ear.
Place the forearm just above the elbow.
Keep the chest facing forward.

limitations: The camera times your stretch only while you're in the position (one arm held across the front of your chest); it does not judge how far you stretch or how long you should hold. Face the phone with your upper body and both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
purpose: Stretch the back of the upper arm and the side of the shoulder.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Stretch gently to a mild pull, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Skip it if raising the arm overhead hurts your shoulder.
instructions: Stand tall and reach one arm up.
Bend the elbow so the hand drops behind your head toward your upper back.
Rest the other hand on the raised elbow and draw it back gently.
Hold for a few slow breaths, release, and switch sides.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the head tall and the elbow beside it.
Keep the ribs down and the core lightly braced.

limitations: The camera times your stretch only while you're in the position (one elbow raised above your head); it does not judge how far you stretch or how long you should hold. Face the phone with your upper body and both arms in view. Experimental.

name: Chest Opener
purpose: Open the chest and the front of the shoulders after pressing work or boxing.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Stretch gently to a mild pull, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Keep the chin level; don't push the head back.
instructions: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart.
Bring the hands together behind your lower back.
Draw the shoulders back and down and let the chest lift a little.
Hold for a few slow breaths, then release.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning back from the lower back
commonMistakes.adjustment: Lift the chest instead and keep the ribs down.
Let them sink away from the ears.

limitations: The camera times your stretch only while you're in the position (standing tall with both hands together behind you); it does not judge how far you stretch or how long you should hold. Face the phone with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
purpose: Stretch the front of the hip, which gets tight from sitting and from lots of leg work.
space: A mat-sized area of clear floor.
equipment: Exercise mat or folded towel under the knee (recommended)
safety: Stretch gently to a mild pull, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Pad the back knee; skip it if kneeling hurts.
instructions: Step one foot back and lower gently onto the back knee, on a mat or towel.
Front knee above the ankle, chest tall, hands on the front thigh.
Tuck the hips under a little and press them gently forward until you feel the front of the back hip stretch.
Hold for a few slow breaths, come up, and switch sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back to go further
commonMistakes.adjustment: Tuck the hips under; a small press is enough.

commonMistakes.mistake: Front knee far past the toes
commonMistakes.adjustment: Move the front foot a little further forward.

limitations: The camera times your stretch only while you're in the position (kneeling on one knee with the chest tall); it does not judge how far you stretch or how long you should hold. Turn the phone sideways and put it at floor level, side-on, with your whole body in view. Experimental.

name: Leg Swings
purpose: Loosen the hips before training with an easy, controlled swing.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Move gently within a comfortable range, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Hold a wall or chair if your balance is unsteady.
instructions: Stand tall on one leg, a hand on a wall or chair if you need it.
Swing the other leg forward and back from the hip, knee soft.
Start small and let the swing grow a little, staying in control.
Do about ten swings, then switch legs.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Let it swing like a pendulum; control the top of each swing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaning back as the leg comes forward
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the chest tall over the standing foot.

commonMistakes.mistake: Arching the back as the leg goes back
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the back swing small and the ribs down.

limitations: The camera does not assess this move yet. Follow the demonstration; the timer guides you. Stand side-on to the phone if you want to watch yourself.

name: Hip Circles
purpose: Warm up the hips and lower back with slow circles.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Move gently within a comfortable range, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness.
instructions: Stand with the feet a little wider than the hips, hands on the hips, knees soft.
Draw slow circles with the hips, keeping the head over the feet.
Do a few circles one way, then the other way.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the upper body quiet; the hips draw the circle.
Take two or three seconds for each circle.

limitations: The camera does not assess this move yet. Follow the demonstration; the timer guides you. Face the phone with your whole body in view.

name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
purpose: Stretch the back of the thigh after leg work or running.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Move gently within a comfortable range, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Keep the back flat; the stretch should be in the back of the thigh, not the lower back.
instructions: Step one heel forward, toes up, front leg long.
Bend the back knee and sit the hips back.
Tip forward from the hips with a flat back, hands resting on the front thigh.
Hold for a few slow breaths, step back in, and switch sides.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach lower
commonMistakes.adjustment: Keep the back flat; tip only as far as the hips allow.
Keep a small softness in the front knee.
Rest the hands on the thigh above the knee.

limitations: The camera does not assess this move yet. Follow the demonstration; the timer guides you. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view.

name: Deep Squat Hold
purpose: Open the hips and ankles by resting in a deep squat.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
equipment: Small plate or book under the heels (optional)
safety: Move gently within a comfortable range, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Go only as low as your knees and hips are comfortable; hold a support if you need it.
instructions: Feet wider than the hips, toes turned out a little.
Sit down between your heels as low as is comfortable, chest up.
Bring the palms together and let the elbows gently press the knees out.
Breathe there, then stand up slowly.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Widen the stance a little or put a thin book under the heels.
Let the elbows guide the knees out over the toes.
Lower slowly and stop where it's comfortable.

limitations: The camera does not assess this move yet. Follow the demonstration; the timer guides you. Face the phone with your whole body in view.

name: Standing Calf Stretch
purpose: Stretch the calves after walking, running, skipping or boxing footwork.
space: About 2 × 2 m of clear, stable, non-slip floor.
safety: Move gently within a comfortable range, never into pain, and breathe slowly. Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling or dizziness. Keep the back heel down without forcing it.
instructions: Step one foot back, toes pointing forward.
Press the back heel down and keep that leg long.
Bend the front knee and lean forward in one line from the back heel to the head, hands on the front thigh.
Hold for a few slow breaths, step in, and switch sides.

commonMistakes.adjustment: Shorten the step until the heel stays down.
Point the back foot straight forward.
Lean the whole body in one line instead.

limitations: The camera does not assess this move yet. Follow the demonstration; the timer guides you. Stand side-on to the phone with your whole body in view.
